objective: COPY-CLASS-20261118-001's referee found one sign that decides SEED's copy step on every run: the fill's far end pair is separated by every crossed split. Freeze it and prove it equivalent to the copy step (sign implies clause (b), and the converse), or find a counterexample; then ask whether the copy class's betweenness reads it. Proof first (what the sign decides on any base and on a base of two orders, and counterexamples off knot-local fills), then a frozen computation on fresh SEEDK runs past the referee's sizes, with an ablation of which pairs must carry knots and a marked five-distinction picture. Serves G1 and G16; challenges A101. Last study on the two-order line.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; refereed R1, confirmed with fixes, no Block; 8 of 8 held, read as two computed facts): on SEEDK's knot-local fills the far-pair sign equals SEED's copy step exactly (149,162 fresh fills, 1,794 copy steps; the referee's 307,135 to n = 64). Not a theorem of the fill: a seven-distinction base of two orders breaks both directions (proved). Proved: under the sign the copy step is 'the moved splits are one whole class', and a pair pattern forces it. The copy class's betweenness does not read the sign; one crossed mark per split on the move's five distinctions does. Every copy step's p lies on the starting line. The two-order line stops.
stop_rule: One proof and one frozen computation with its read-out; referee hand-off; report; the line stops.
title: Is the far pair's sign SEED's copy step?
